title_en: Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. v. Shanxi Provincial Cardiovascular Disease Hospital (Third Party: Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.) — dispute over a Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 14 of the Implementing Regulations for the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-foreign Equity Joint Ventures provides that: 'A joint venture agreement, contract, and articles of association shall become effective upon approval by the examination and approval authority, and the same applies to their amendments.' A supplementary agreement reached by the parties during the performance of a joint venture agreement or contract, although constituting an amendment to the original contract, shall have its validity comprehensively analyzed in light of the facts of the case. If the content of the supplementary agreement does not involve matters that must be submitted to the examination and approval authority for approval and does not constitute a substantive change to the already approved joint venture agreement, a party's claim that the content of the supplementary agreement is invalid solely on the ground that it has not been approved by the examination and approval authority shall not be supported by the people's court.

Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. v. Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital, and Third Party Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Contract

Ruling Summary

Article 14 of the Implementation Regulations of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures provides: "The joint venture agreement, contract and articles of association shall become effective after being approved by the approval authority, and the same applies to any amendments thereto." A supplementary agreement reached by the parties in the course of performing a joint venture agreement or contract, although constituting an amendment to the original contract, should be analyzed comprehensively in light of the facts of the case when determining its validity. If the contents of the supplementary agreement do not involve matters that must be submitted to the approval authority for examination and approval, and do not substantially alter the approved joint venture agreement, a court shall not support a party's claim that the contents of the supplementary agreement are invalid solely on the ground that the supplementary agreement has not been approved by the approval authority.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 3

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 57 Paterson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Cui Cheng, Chairman of the Company.
Authorized Agent: Wang Chun, Attorney at Beijing Shanggong Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital, domiciled at No. 18 Yifen Street, Wanbailin District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Li Bao, President of the Hospital.
Authorized Agents: Li Fei, Attorney at Shanxi Huanghe Law Firm; Wu Xiaofeng, Attorney at Shanxi Huanghe Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 308 Pingyang Road, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Wang Jianming, Chairman of the Company.

Regarding the dispute over a Sino-foreign equity joint venture contract between appellant Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jincheng Company) and appellant Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital (hereinafter referred to as Cardiovascular Hospital), and the third party at first instance Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huanneng Company), the Shanxi High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) rendered the Civil Judgment (2008) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 12 on November 23, 2009. Both Jincheng Company and Cardiovascular Hospital disagreed with the judgment and appealed to this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with trial judge Lu Xiaolong serving as presiding judge, and trial judges Xi Xiangyang and acting trial judge Yang Honglei participating in the review. A public hearing was held on April 20, 2010. Cui Cheng, legal representative of Jincheng Company, and its authorized agent Wang Chun, as well as Li Fei and Wu Xiaofeng, authorized agents of Cardiovascular Hospital, appeared in court for the proceedings. The third party at first instance, Huanneng Company, having been legally summoned by this Court, failed to send any representative to appear in court. This case is now concluded.

Jincheng Company initiated a lawsuit at the court of first instance, alleging: The plaintiff and the defendant signed a "Letter of Intent for Cooperation" at the "2006 Shanxi (Hong Kong) Investment Seminar" in August 2006, regarding the "Shanxi Cardiovascular Hospital and Senior Care and Rehabilitation Project" (hereinafter referred to as the cooperation project). On November 18 of the same year, based on the requirements of Cardiovascular Hospital and the equipment list provided by it, the plaintiff entered into a contract for the purchase of medical equipment with Hong Kong Baohe Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baohe Company), and subsequently paid commissions and advance payments totaling HKD 45,122,800. In November of the same year, the plaintiff, the defendant, and the third party signed the "Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Joint Venture Contract") and the "Articles of Association of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture" (hereinafter referred to as the "Articles of Association"). In December of the same year, upon examination and approval by the relevant functional departments of the Shanxi Provincial People's Government, the three joint venture parties jointly established the Sino-foreign equity joint venture enterprise Shanxi Jiufang Health Industry Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiufang Company or the joint venture company). In January 2007, the joint venture company obtained the "Business License of Enterprise Legal Person." On February 25 of the same year, the three joint venture parties jointly signed a "Memorandum" stipulating that Cardiovascular Hospital should expedite the procedures for contributing land as capital, and complete them before June 2007. However, Cardiovascular Hospital failed to fulfill this obligation. At the end of September of the same year, it orally notified the plaintiff that the cooperation project and the joint venture company were to cease operations. At the plaintiff's request, it sent a letter on November 16 of the same year, stating that due to the inability to complete the land procedures, the cooperation project was terminated. On January 22, 2008, Cardiovascular Hospital and the third party Huanneng Company signed a "Memorandum on the Return of Investment Funds to Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.," acknowledging that Cardiovascular Hospital had unilaterally terminated the project cooperation and returned its investment of RMB 2,619,700. Due to Cardiovascular Hospital's breach of contract, the sales contract between the plaintiff and Baohe Company could not be further performed. After failed negotiations, Baohe Company filed a lawsuit in the Court of First Instance of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, requesting the plaintiff to bear liability for breach of contract. The High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region ultimately ruled that the plaintiff should pay compensation of HKD 23,622,800 to Baohe Company. After the occurrence of the defendant's breach, the plaintiff repeatedly proposed to the defendant the handling of post-termination matters of the cooperation project, especially the compensation for the plaintiff's losses. However, the defendant adopted a prevaricating and passive attitude, resulting in the inability of all parties to communicate and reaching no consensus to date. The plaintiff had no choice but to seek relief through litigation. The plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Order the defendant to pay liquidated damages, including liquidated damages for delayed capital contribution under Article 14.1 of the Joint Venture Contract in the amount of RMB 2,814,750, and liquidated damages under Article 14.2 based on the defendant's fault leading to the inability to perform the Joint Venture Contract, in the amount of RMB 22.5 million (calculated at 15% of the registered capital under the Joint Venture Contract); 2. Order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for losses, including losses arising from the purchase of medical equipment for the cooperation project in the amount of RMB 23,764,064.34, interest losses on the funds already paid for the purchase of medical equipment (principal of HKD 45,122,800, converted to RMB 45,392,600, calculated from December 25, 2006, to August 31, 2008, at the benchmark interest rate for working capital loans of the People's Bank of China during the same period), and the plaintiff's preliminary expenses of RMB 3 million; 3. Order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for loss of prospective profits in the amount of RMB 10 million; 4. Bear all litigation costs of this case.

Cardiovascular Hospital defended as follows: (A) Jincheng Company failed to make its capital contribution in full and on time, and thus lacks the standing to claim liability for breach of contract or damages from the defendant. All its claims have no legal basis. Article 28, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 7 of the "Several Provisions on Capital Contributions by the Parties to a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture" approved by the State Council on December 30, 1987, all provide that only the non-breaching party who has made full and timely capital contributions may request other breaching parties to bear liability for breach of contract or damages. In this case, Jincheng Company was required to contribute RMB 60 million (including RMB 30 million in cash and RMB 30 million in equipment). By the final deadline for capital contributions, Jincheng Company had made zero cash contributions and had not delivered the equipment. Jincheng Company is not a non-breaching party, but a breaching party, and thus lacks the standing to pursue liability for breach of contract or damages from any other shareholder, including the defendant. (B) Apart from lacking legal standing, all of Jincheng Company's claims also violate other legal provisions, are inconsistent with the facts or the agreed terms, or lack evidentiary support. Specifically: 1. The agreement in the joint venture company's "Memorandum" dated February 25, 2007, to change the deadline for capital contributions, is not effective because it was not approved by the approval authority. Therefore, Jincheng Company's request for payment of RMB 2,814,750 in liquidated damages under Article 14.1 of the Joint Venture Contract has no legal or factual basis. 2. Article 14.2 of the Joint Venture Contract applies to breaches other than failure to make capital contributions and is conditional on fault. Cardiovascular Hospital had no fault regarding the joint venture company's failure to obtain the land use rights. Jincheng Company also failed to provide any evidence that Cardiovascular Hospital had any other breaches. Moreover, calculating liquidated damages at 15% of the total registered capital of the joint venture company has no legal basis. Therefore, Jincheng Company's request for payment of RMB 22.5 million in liquidated damages under Article 14.2 of the Joint Venture Contract also has no legal or factual basis. 3. Jincheng Company's claim for damages for the loss of equipment purchase costs of RMB 23,764,064.34 and interest losses of RMB 5,813,900 is based on the wrong party in the lawsuit, and the evidence lacks relevance, authenticity, and mutual corroboration, violating the rules of civil evidence. Jincheng Company's obligation to contribute equipment as capital was owed to Jiufang Company, not to Cardiovascular Hospital. Jincheng Company should make this claim against Jiufang Company, not Cardiovascular Hospital. According to Order 42, rule 5B of the Rules of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, "The court shall, at the time of pronouncing the judgment or order, state the reasons for any relevant decision." However, the "Consent Order" does not record the court's reasons or the nature of the liability assumed. Although this Consent Order was notarized by a Hong Kong lawyer recognized by the Ministry of Justice of the PRC, this merely pertains to the procedural matter of judicial assistance and only attests to the formal authenticity of the Consent Order. Therefore, the Consent Order of the Court of First Instance of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region dated July 24, 2008, in case HCA808/2008, has no relevance to this case and cannot prove the authenticity of the creditor-debtor relationship between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, and should not be admitted as evidence. The evidence submitted by Jincheng Company regarding its equipment transaction does not mutually corroborate, lacks authenticity, and should not be admitted as evidence. Even if there were losses from the equipment purchase, Jincheng Company bears significant fault for the occurrence of the losses. 4. Jincheng Company's request for return of the preliminary expenses of RMB 3 million cannot be supported. Jincheng Company has not submitted any evidence of the RMB 3 million investment. Even if RMB 3 million was invested, according to corporate law principles, it should be borne by the established Jiufang Company. The agreed provision is voidable due to gross unfairness. The joint venture company has been legally registered, and thus the conditions for "failure to register" under Article 14.3 of the Joint Venture Contract are not met. Since the provision is to be applied under Article 14.1, Cardiovascular Hospital has no obligation to Jincheng Company, which is also a breaching party. 5. Jincheng Company's claim for RMB 10 million in loss of prospective profits based on investment promotion advertisements and government documents has no factual or legal basis. Prospective profits refer to the expected benefits a non-breaching party could have obtained under the contract. Jincheng Company is a breaching party and is not entitled to performance benefits or expectation interests under the law, and thus has no right to claim damages for loss of prospective profits. The "Shanxi Key Investment Promotion Projects," which are essentially promotional materials, and the government approval documents for project establishment, are not the basis for determining or calculating loss of prospective profits. Business operations are fraught with uncertainties, and it is unpredictable that a company would only generate profits without going bankrupt. (C) Jiufang Company and all its shareholders have suffered severe losses. The cause of the losses is not any shareholder's breach of contract, but objective reasons that were unforeseeable and insurmountable. On September 30, 2007, the Shanxi Provincial Health Department convened a meeting with the principal responsible persons of Cardiovascular Hospital, announcing the cessation of the joint venture project, and established a post-termination working leadership group comprising departmental leaders and the main responsible persons of Cardiovascular Hospital. While Cardiovascular Hospital exerted its utmost efforts to handle the land procedures and had no fault whatsoever, the relevant government departments failed to approve the contribution of land as capital. This not only eliminated the basis for the continued performance of the Joint Venture Contract but also caused losses to the joint venture company and all shareholders. The defendant maintains that the cause of the losses was not any shareholder's breach of contract; all shareholders are victims. Under these circumstances, imposing the consequences of the losses on only one shareholder clearly contradicts the facts of this case and the relevant legal provisions. In summary, all of Jincheng Company's claims should be dismissed.

The third party Huanneng Company stated: Huanneng Company and Cardiovascular Hospital signed and fully performed the "Memorandum on the Return of Investment Funds to Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd." on January 22, 2008. Accordingly, Huanneng Company has transferred all its rights and obligations under the original Joint Venture Contract to Cardiovascular Hospital. All rights and obligations of Huanneng Company involved in this case should be borne by Cardiovascular Hospital. The plaintiff Jincheng Company has made no specific claims against Huanneng Company, and Huanneng Company has no substantial relationship with the dispute in this case.

The court of first instance, after trial, found the following facts: On July 27, 2006, at the "2006 Shanxi (Hong Kong) Investment Seminar," Jincheng Company and Cardiovascular Hospital signed a "Letter of Intent for Cooperation" concerning the "Shanxi Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Senior Care and Rehabilitation Center" project. It stipulated that Cardiovascular Hospital was responsible for handling the approval procedures for the transfer of land use rights related to the project and for conducting an appraisal of the land use rights.

On November 10 of the same year, Cardiovascular Hospital sent a letter to Jincheng Company entitled "Letter on the Demand for Imported Equipment Investment for the Shanxi Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Senior Rehabilitation Center Project," stating that to ensure the smooth implementation of the cooperation project, it would provide a list of medical equipment with a total price of RMB 123.1 million, to be directly purchased and invested by Jincheng Company.

On November 18 of the same year, based on Cardiovascular Hospital's requirements and the equipment list provided, the buyer Jincheng Company and the seller Baohe Company entered into a contract for the purchase of medical equipment, numbered HY20061118. Article 10 of the contract: Within 30 days after the conclusion of the contract, the buyer shall pay the seller a 35% advance payment of the total contract price in installments. The buyer shall also pay a commission of 5% of the total contract price in a lump sum within 30 days. The buyer and seller shall separately sign and handle the relevant contract and procedures for pledging 50 million shares of the buyer as collateral to the seller. Article 11: If the buyer fails to perform the above obligations, the seller has the right to revoke or terminate the contract in whole or in part, without the buyer's consent and without any compensation to the buyer. The buyer shall pay the seller liquidated damages equal to 25% of the total contract price and bear all losses caused by the breach. The 5% commission paid by the buyer to the seller shall not be refunded. Article 20: ... For whatever reason, if the buyer terminates this contract, in whole or in part, the notice of termination must be sent to the seller in writing. Upon such notice, the seller shall stop work, and the buyer shall pay the seller the contract price for all goods that have already been manufactured, modified, or ordered by the seller prior to the termination and that conform to the contract. Such goods shall be delivered to the buyer.

On November 30 of the same year, Jincheng Company, Cardiovascular Hospital, and Huanneng Company signed the "Joint Venture Contract" and the "Articles of Association." The main contents of the Joint Venture Contract were: Article 6 Registered Capital, Total Investment, and Investment Methods. 6.1 Registered capital: RMB 150 million. 6.2 Investment methods: Cardiovascular Hospital, RMB 67.5 million, to be contributed in the form of land of equivalent value; Jincheng Company, RMB 60 million, including RMB 30 million in cash and RMB 30 million in equipment; Huanneng Company, RMB 22.5 million in cash. Articles 6.3 to 6.5 stipulated the deadlines for the three shareholders to make their capital contributions in installments, with the final deadline being 18 months after the registration of the joint venture company. Article 7 Responsibilities of Each Party. 7.1 Responsibilities of Cardiovascular Hospital: To contribute registered capital in accordance with Article 6; to be responsible for handling all procedures for the transfer of land use rights for the project and bearing all related costs. 7.2 Responsibilities of Jincheng Company: To contribute registered capital in accordance with Article 6; to recommend and purchase necessary machinery and equipment from overseas for the joint venture company. Article 14 Liability for Breach of Contract. 14.1 If any one of Party A, Party B, or Party C fails to make the agreed amount of investment on time in accordance with the provisions of Article 6 of this contract, counting from the 30th banking day after the overdue date, for each day of delay, the breaching party shall pay liquidated damages equal to 0.5‰ of the amount of investment. In addition, the non-breaching party shall have the right to terminate this contract in accordance with the provisions of Article 17 and claim damages from the breaching party. 14.2 If, due to the fault of one party, this contract and its appendices cannot be performed or cannot be fully performed, the party at fault shall bear liability for breach of contract; if it is due to the fault of three parties, each party shall bear its respective liability for breach of contract according to the actual circumstances. 14.3 After all parties sign this contract, if Cardiovascular Hospital fails to complete the procedures for contributing land as capital on time, causing the joint venture company to be unable to register, it shall be deemed a breach by Cardiovascular Hospital. This shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of Article 14.1, and Cardiovascular Hospital shall also return the RMB 3 million already invested by Jincheng Company and compensate for the losses from equipment ordering. Article 15 Amendment, Termination, and Rescission of the Contract. 15.1 Any amendment to this contract and its appendices must be subject to a written agreement signed by all three parties and submitted to the original approval authority for approval before it becomes effective. 15.3 If, for some reason, the joint venture company suffers successive losses and is unable to continue operations, upon a unanimous resolution of the board of directors and approval by the original approval authority, the joint venture term may be terminated early or the contract may be rescinded. The main contents of the Articles of Association were: 3.3 Party A, Party B, and Party C shall pay their respective capital contributions in full within the time limits stipulated in the contract. 10.4 If, for some reason, the joint venture company suffers successive losses and is unable to continue operations, upon a unanimous resolution of the board of directors and approval by the original approval authority, the joint venture term may be terminated early or the contract may be rescinded. 12.1 Any amendment to these Articles of Association must be subject to a unanimous resolution of the board of directors and reported to the original approval authority for approval. 12.3 These Articles of Association shall take effect only after approval by the Shanxi Provincial Department of Commerce; the same applies to their amendments.

In December of the same year, upon examination and approval by the relevant functional departments of the Shanxi Provincial People's Government, the three parties jointly established the Sino-foreign equity joint venture enterprise — Jiufang Company. Jiufang Company obtained the "Business License of Enterprise Legal Person" on January 9, 2007. According to the Joint Venture Contract and the Articles of Association, the final deadline for all three shareholders to make their full registered capital contributions was 18 months after the registration of the joint venture company, i.e., July 9, 2008.

On February 25, 2007, the three shareholders of the joint venture company jointly signed a "Memorandum" of Jiufang Company, the main contents of which were: 1. Cardiovascular Hospital shall expedite the procedures for contributing land as capital and complete the relevant land procedures before the end of June 2007. 2. Jincheng Company has completed the ordering of equipment as agreed, and shall inject funds in due course according to the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. The three parties agreed to adjust the timing and amount of capital contributions from each party based on the actual progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. Implementing in accordance with the above principles, all parties would be deemed to have fulfilled their capital contribution obligations.

At the end of September of the same year, Cardiovascular Hospital orally notified Jincheng Company that the cooperation project and the joint venture company were to "cease operations." On October 28 of the same year, Jincheng Company sent a letter to Cardiovascular Hospital requesting "a formal written notice regarding the cessation of operations of the joint venture company." On November 16 of the same year, Cardiovascular Hospital sent a letter to Jincheng Company titled "Letter on the Termination of Implementation and Resolution of Post-Termination Matters for the Shanxi Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Senior Care and Rehabilitation Center Project," stating: "Due to unclear policy boundaries and other reasons, the land procedures could not be completed, resulting in the termination of the project."

After the Cardiovascular Hospital notified the “termination of project implementation,” Jincheng Company sent three letters to Baohe Company on October 29, November 20, and December 18 of the same year, respectively, to negotiate matters related to the termination of the contract. Baohe Company’s letter ultimately proposed a claim for compensation for breach of contract at “a ratio of no less than 15% of the total contract amount.”

On January 22, 2008, the Cardiovascular Hospital and Huanneng Company signed the *Memorandum on the Return of Investment Funds of Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.*, which stated: The Cardiovascular Hospital unilaterally terminated the project cooperation and agreed to return RMB 2,619,700 in investment funds to Huanneng Company.

In April of the same year, Baohe Company initiated proceedings in the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Court of First Instance, requesting Jincheng Company to bear liability for breach of contract. On July 24 of the same year, the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region issued an *Order* with the following content: Based on the joint request of Baohe Company and Jincheng Company, both parties agreed to the following: 1. The court ruled that the debt would be borne by Jincheng Company; 2. Jincheng Company must pay Baohe Company a total of HKD 23,622,800; 3. No court costs were imposed.

The court of first instance held: There were three issues in dispute in this case: First, whether Jincheng Company’s claim for liquidated damages could be established and the specific amount thereof; second, whether Jincheng Company’s claim for compensation for losses could be established and the specific amount thereof; third, whether Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 10 million in lost profits could be established.

Regarding the first issue: (i) Jincheng Company requested RMB 2,814,750 in liquidated damages from the Cardiovascular Hospital under Article 14.1 of the *Joint Venture Contract*. The court of first instance held: First, Article 28, Paragraph 1 of the *Company Law of the People’s Republic of China* provides: “A shareholder shall make capital contributions in the amount and within the time limit subscribed in the articles of association. Where a shareholder makes capital contributions in currency, he shall deposit the full amount of monetary contributions into a bank account opened by the limited liability company; where a shareholder makes capital contributions with non-monetary property, he shall go through the formalities for the transfer of property rights in accordance with the law.” Paragraph 2 of the same Article provides: “If a shareholder fails to make the capital contribution in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, in addition to paying the full contribution to the company, he shall also bear the liability for breach of contract to the shareholders who have made their capital contributions in full and on time.” Article 14.1 of the *Joint Venture Contract* signed by the three parties stipulates: “If any party among Party A, Party B, and Party C fails to make its capital contributions in the amount and within the time limit specified in Article 6 of this contract, … the complying party has the right to demand the breaching party to compensate for losses.” Given that the Cardiovascular Hospital failed to fulfill its obligation to pay RMB 40.5 million in cash within six months after the registration of the joint venture company, Jincheng Company also failed to fulfill its obligation to pay its cash contribution of RMB 20 million on time. Jincheng Company was not a qualified subject to assert the claim. Second, although Jincheng Company denied its own breach by invoking the agreement among the three shareholders in the *Memorandum* to “inject funds at an opportune time,” under Article 28, Paragraph 1 of the *Company Law of the People’s Republic of China*, shareholders’ subscribed capital contributions shall be fully paid on time. The agreement to “inject funds at an opportune time” changed the capital contribution deadlines established in the *Joint Venture Contract* and the *Joint Venture Articles of Association* from definite to indefinite, which harmed the interests of Jiufang Company and violated mandatory provisions of the Company Law. Therefore, the agreement to “inject funds at an opportune time” should be deemed invalid. Making capital contributions in full and on time is a statutory obligation of shareholders, and Jincheng Company could not use any reason to exempt or delay the performance of its capital contribution obligation. That is to say, Jincheng Company, as the breaching party, had no right to claim RMB 2,814,750 in liquidated damages from the Cardiovascular Hospital.

(ii) Jincheng Company requested the Cardiovascular Hospital to pay RMB 22.5 million in liquidated damages under Article 14.2 of the *Joint Venture Contract*, calculated at 15% of the subject matter of the contract (registered capital of RMB 150 million). The court of first instance held: Since Article 14.1 of the *Joint Venture Contract* stipulates the liability for breach regarding capital contribution, the provisions of Article 14.2 apply to other breaches except those involving capital contributions. The Cardiovascular Hospital’s termination of the project was due to its inability to fulfill its capital contribution obligation by contributing land as equity, and there was no other breach of contract. Moreover, this provision did not specify liquidated damages or the method for calculating liquidated damages. Jincheng Company’s calculation of liquidated damages based on 15% of the total registered capital of the joint venture company lacked legal basis. In summary, Jincheng Company’s claim for liquidated damages could not be established, and the court of first instance did not support it.

Regarding the second issue: Jincheng Company claimed compensation for three types of losses: an initial investment of RMB 3 million, interest losses on payments converted to RMB 5.8139 million, and compensation paid to Baohe Company converted to RMB 23,764,064.34.

(i) Whether Jincheng Company’s claim for compensation for losses could be established. First, liquidated damages are a form of compensation agreed upon by the parties in the contract for breach of contract. Article 14.3 of the *Joint Venture Contract* signed by the three shareholders expressly stipulates: “If Party A (the Cardiovascular Hospital) fails to complete the formalities for contributing land as equity within the time limit, rendering the joint venture company unable to be registered, it shall be deemed that Party A has breached the contract. The provisions of Article 14.1 shall apply, and Party A shall also return the RMB 3 million already invested by Party B (Jincheng Company) and compensate for losses from equipment orders.” Therefore, Jincheng Company’s claim, because it was stipulated in the contract, was also a claim for liquidated damages. Although the application of Article 14.3 is conditioned on “the Cardiovascular Hospital failing to complete the land equity contribution formalities within the time limit, rendering the joint venture company unable to be registered,” the objective fact in this case was that Jiufang Company had already been established despite zero capital contributions from the Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company. Since the land equity contribution was impossible, the Cardiovascular Hospital had notified the termination of the cooperation project, and the joint venture company could not operate. Therefore, the Cardiovascular Hospital’s defense that it was not liable because the joint venture company had been established could not be sustained. Second, after the Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company signed the *Letter of Intent for Cooperation* on November 10, 2006, the Cardiovascular Hospital sent Jincheng Company a “Letter on Investment Demand for Imported Equipment for Shanxi Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Rehabilitation Nursing Home Project,” providing a list of medical equipment with a total price of RMB 123.1 million, for Jincheng Company to purchase and invest directly. Jincheng Company then signed a *Contract* with Baohe Company for the purchase of medical equipment in accordance with the Cardiovascular Hospital’s requirements and the provided list. On November 30, 2006, Jincheng Company, the Cardiovascular Hospital, and Huanneng Company signed the *Joint Venture Contract* and *Joint Venture Articles of Association*. The *Joint Venture Contract* clearly stated that Jincheng Company’s capital contribution of RMB 60 million comprised RMB 30 million in cash and RMB 30 million in equipment; Jincheng Company had the responsibility to recommend the purchase of necessary machinery and equipment overseas for the joint venture company; and if the Cardiovascular Hospital failed to complete the land equity contribution formalities within the time limit, it would be liable for losses from Jincheng Company’s equipment orders. In particular, the *Memorandum* signed by the three shareholders of the joint venture company on February 25, 2007, clearly recorded that Jincheng Company had completed the equipment orders as agreed. The above evidence was sufficient to prove that due to the termination of the cooperation project, Jincheng Company suffered actual losses from the equipment purchase. Pursuant to Article 107 of the *Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China*, which provides that “Where a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach of contract,” the Cardiovascular Hospital failed to perform its obligation to contribute land as equity, which led to the termination of the cooperation project and caused actual losses to Jincheng Company. The Cardiovascular Hospital should compensate Jincheng Company for the losses from the equipment purchase. Therefore, Jincheng Company’s claim for compensation for losses was established.

(ii) The determination of the specific amount of Jincheng Company’s compensation for losses. First, with respect to Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 5.8139 million in interest losses arising from the HKD 45.1228 million payment. The court of first instance held: (a) There were numerous issues with the evidence provided by Jincheng Company: 1. The contents of the *Contract* between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company were consistent between the copy and the original, but the formats differed; 2. The receipts issued by Baohe Company to Jincheng Company included copies and stubs, but no originals; 3. The letter sent by Jincheng Company to Baohe Company on October 29, 2007, stated that Jincheng Company had, on December 13, 2006, paid 35% of the total contract amount as advance payment and 5% of the total contract amount as commission, i.e., HKD 45.1228 million. However, the receipts showed that as of December 13, 2006, Jincheng Company had not paid the commission and the total payment was only HKD 29.5 million; 4. The reply letter sent by Baohe Company to Jincheng Company on November 16 stated, “Your letter of November 20 has been received.” (b) Jincheng Company failed to provide important evidence that could prove its losses from the equipment purchase: 1. The letter sent by Jincheng Company to Baohe Company on December 18, 2007, proved that a *Supplementary Agreement* was signed between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company on January 15, 2007, but it was not provided; 2. According to the receipts, Jincheng Company had paid Baohe Company HKD 45.1228 million, but the Hong Kong *Order* ordered Jincheng Company to pay only HKD 23.6228 million. Therefore, Jincheng Company should have evidence of Baohe Company’s refund of HKD 21.5 million, but such evidence was not provided; 3. Article 10 of the *Contract* between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company stipulated that both parties would separately sign and process a share mortgage contract for 50 million shares and related formalities, but this was not provided. … Based on this, the court of first instance did not support this claim. Second, with respect to Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 23,764,064.34 in compensation paid to Baohe Company pursuant to the *Order* of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The court of first instance held: The *Order* issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was a consent order made based on the joint request of Baohe Company and Jincheng Company and their mutual agreement. The High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region did not conduct a substantive trial of the sales contract relationship between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company. Moreover, even if the *Order* of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was authentic, legal, and valid, its effect could only bind the parties to the *Order*, i.e., Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, and did not have legal binding force on third parties such as the Cardiovascular Hospital. Therefore, the court of first instance did not support this claim. Third, with respect to Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 3 million in initial investment. The court of first instance held: Jincheng Company relied on the *Joint Venture Contract* signed by the three shareholders. The *Joint Venture Contract* was voluntarily signed by the three shareholders on the principle of equality and mutual benefit, and represented the true intent of the three shareholders. The *Joint Venture Contract* was approved by the Shanxi Provincial Department of Commerce and was legal and valid. Article 14.3 of the *Joint Venture Contract* clearly stipulates: “If Party A (the Cardiovascular Hospital) fails to complete the formalities for contributing land as equity within the time limit, rendering the joint venture company unable to be registered, it shall be deemed that Party A has breached the contract. The provisions of Article 14.1 shall apply, and Party A shall also return the RMB 3 million already invested by Party B (Jincheng Company) and compensate for losses from equipment orders.” Therefore, the court of first instance supported Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 3 million in initial investment.

Finally, the determination of the amount of Jincheng Company’s compensation for losses. The court of first instance, after comprehensive comparison, held: The Cardiovascular Hospital, by failing to fulfill its obligation to contribute land as equity and unilaterally terminating the cooperation project, caused actual losses to Jincheng Company and should bear liability for breach of contract. Jincheng Company had defects in its evidence proving the actual losses from the purchase of medical equipment and should also bear some responsibility. Its claims for interest on the payment and for compensation determined by the *Order* could not be supported. Based on the existence of actual losses and considering the degree of fault of both parties, and in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith, the court of first instance, in its discretion, ordered the Cardiovascular Hospital to bear liability for breach of contract in the amount of 15% of the HKD 45.1228 million in medical equipment payments claimed by Jincheng Company, i.e., to pay Jincheng Company RMB 6,788,420 in liquidated damages.

Regarding the third issue: The court of first instance held: First, the amount of compensation for lost profits should be related to the degree of performance of the contract. Where the Cardiovascular Hospital breached the contract by failing to contribute land as equity, Jincheng Company also violated the statutory capital contribution obligation under the *Company Law of the People’s Republic of China* by not fulfilling its contribution obligation. According to the *Company Law of the People’s Republic of China*, shareholders can only enjoy dividends based on their capital contributions. Given that Jincheng Company made no capital contribution, it could not obtain expected returns. Second, lost profits must have a realistic material basis. In this case, none of the three shareholders made capital contributions, the cooperation project was terminated, and Jiufang Company could not operate, let alone generate profits. Third, although the *Key Investment Promotion Projects of Shanxi Province* made very clear and definite predictions about the expected returns of the cooperation project, the *Joint Venture Contract* and *Joint Venture Articles of Association* signed by the three parties stipulated that “if the joint venture company incurs consecutive losses due to certain reasons and is unable to continue operations, upon unanimous adoption by the board of directors and approval by the original approving authority, the joint venture term may be terminated early or the contract may be rescinded.” That is, high returns also come with high risks. Lost profits cannot be claimed based on uncertain expectations. Therefore, Jincheng Company’s claim for RMB 10 million in lost profits could not be established, and the court of first instance did not support it.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 5, 6, 107, 114, and 120 of the *Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China*, and Article 28 of the *Company Law of the People’s Republic of China*, rendered the following judgment: 1. The Cardiovascular Hospital shall pay Jincheng Company RMB 3 million as liquidated damages for initial investment within 30 days after the judgment takes effect; 2. The Cardiovascular Hospital shall pay Jincheng Company RMB 6,788,420 as liquidated damages for losses from medical equipment within 30 days after the judgment takes effect; 3. All other claims of Jincheng Company are rejected. The case acceptance fee of RMB 381,263 shall be borne by the Cardiovascular Hospital in the amount of RMB 281,263 and by Jincheng Company in the amount of RMB 100,000.

Both Jincheng Company and the Cardiovascular Hospital disagreed with the above judgment of the court of first instance and appealed to this Court.

Jincheng Company appealed, claiming: (1) The appellee, Cardiovascular Hospital, seriously violated the provisions of the "Joint Venture Contract", failing to handle the land-for-equity transfer procedures, rendering the cooperation project impossible to proceed, and thus should bear fundamental liability for breach of contract. The first-instance judgment erred in determining the liability for breach of contract of both parties. Article 14.1 of the "Joint Venture Contract" stipulates the liability of shareholders for breach of contract, Article 14.2 stipulates the liability for breach where the contract cannot be performed or fully performed due to the fault of one party, and Article 14.3 further specifically defines the fundamental liability for breach of contract on the part of Party A, Cardiovascular Hospital, regarding the land not being contributed as equity. Cardiovascular Hospital was required to deliver at least RMB 40,500,000 in cash within six months after the registration of the joint venture company, but it never paid the cash contribution, nor did it contribute the land use rights as equity within the time specified in the "Memorandum", clearly violating the shareholders' capital contribution obligations. It unilaterally notified the project to cease operations on November 16, 2007. Calculated at 0.5‰ per day, for the period from June 30, 2006, to November 16, 2007, totaling 139 days, liquidated damages should be RMB 2,814,750. In addition to paying liquidated damages under Article 14.1 of the "Joint Venture Contract", Cardiovascular Hospital, having seriously breached the contract and rendered the cooperation project impossible, should also pay 15% of the total contract amount as liquidated damages, amounting to RMB 22,500,000. (2) The first-instance judgment's finding that the appellant, not having fully contributed capital under the contract, had no right to demand that Cardiovascular Hospital bear liability for breach, is inconsistent with the facts. As early as November 18, 2006, Jincheng Company, at the request of Cardiovascular Hospital and based on the equipment list provided, signed a contract with Baohe Company for the purchase of medical equipment valued at over RMB 100 million, and paid HKD 45,122,800 in cash, with the balance offset by a pledge of equity. The equipment was ready for customs declaration at any time. On February 25, 2007, the three shareholders of the joint venture company jointly signed the "Memorandum", which confirmed that Jincheng Company had completed the equipment ordering, and changed the original payment method to cash payment based on the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. Therefore, Jincheng Company contributed capital as agreed by the three shareholders, and there was no breach in its capital contribution. Jincheng Company is entitled to claim liability for breach of contract against Cardiovascular Hospital. (3) The first-instance judgment erred in determining the appellant's actual losses. Due to Cardiovascular Hospital's breach, the project was completely impossible to proceed, and Jincheng Company's contract for the purchase of equipment also became impossible to perform. After repeated unsuccessful negotiations with the equipment supplier, Baohe Company, Baohe Company sued Jincheng Company in Hong Kong and demanded substantial compensation. Subsequently, through multiple rounds of negotiations between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, Jincheng Company minimized the losses to the greatest extent possible. On July 24, 2008, the Court of First Instance of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region issued Order No. 808, ordering Jincheng Company to compensate Baohe Company for losses of HKD 23,622,800, equivalent to RMB 23,764,064.34. Cardiovascular Hospital should compensate for these actual losses that have already occurred. The first-instance court, disregarding the fact that the "Memorandum" had confirmed Jincheng Company's completion of the ordering obligation, repeatedly questioned the contractual exchanges between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, denied the actual losses suffered by Jincheng Company, and denied that the "Order" of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was the result of the handling of the equipment ordering case by that court. The first-instance court's finding that the "Order" was not binding on Cardiovascular Hospital is completely erroneous. During the first instance, after the trial, Jincheng Company, at the request of the court, again provided receipts issued by Baohe Company and the certification of its legal representative. However, Cardiovascular Hospital refused to cross-examine on the grounds that the evidence was submitted beyond the time limit. Jincheng Company believes that submitting additional evidence at the court's request does not violate the rules of evidence, and the above evidence can fully prove the legal relationship between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company and the payment of funds by Jincheng Company. Cardiovascular Hospital should compensate Jincheng Company for the interest losses on the funds paid for the equipment. (4) Cardiovascular Hospital should compensate the appellant for the expected profit losses suffered due to the inability to perform the cooperative project. This project was a key promotion project of Shanxi Province. According to the "Key Investment Promotion Projects of Shanxi Province" issued by the Shanxi Provincial People's Government department, which contained full and reasonable predictions of the project's income, it stated that "after the project is completed, each bed/year can generate a profit of USD 1.25." According to the "Reply on the Approval of the Joint Venture Project of Shanxi Provincial Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Rehabilitation and Nursing Center" (Jin Fa Gai Wai Zi [2007] No. 88) approved by the Shanxi Provincial Development and Reform Commission, the cooperative project should have 500 beds. Based on this calculation, after the project is completed, Jincheng Company, as a shareholder holding 40% equity, would have an expected profit of RMB 17,080,000. The appellant only requests Cardiovascular Hospital to pay RMB 10,000,000 for expected profit. In summary, the first-instance court misapprehended the facts and erred in admitting evidence. The appellant respectfully requests the court of second instance to ascertain the facts in accordance with the law and amend the judgment. Request: 1. Set aside items 2 and 3 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2008) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Shanxi High People's Court; 2. Amend the judgment to order the appellee to bear liquidated damages of RMB 22,500,000 for its fault leading to the inability to perform the "Joint Venture Contract", and liquidated damages of RMB 2,814,750 for failing to contribute capital as agreed in the "Joint Venture Contract"; 3. Amend the judgment to order the appellee to compensate the appellant for actual losses of RMB 23,764,064.34 incurred from the purchase of medical equipment for the cooperative project, and interest losses of RMB 5,813,900 on the paid amounts (principal of HKD 45,122,800 paid for equipment, converted to RMB 45,392,600; calculated from December 25, 2006, temporarily to August 31, 2008, at the loan interest rate for the same period set by the People's Bank of China); 4. Amend the judgment to order the appellee to compensate the appellant for lost expected profit of RMB 10,000,000.

Cardiovascular Hospital appealed, claiming: (1) In the absence of any evidence of the appellee's initial investment of RMB 3,000,000, the first-instance judgment ordered the appellant to bear liquidated damages of RMB 3,000,000. This not only misapprehended the facts but also contradicted other findings in the judgment. The first-instance judgment confused liquidated damages with compensation for losses, two different forms of liability, transforming compensation into liquidated damages and relieving the appellee of the burden of proof regarding the RMB 3,000,000 investment. Article 14.3 of the "Joint Venture Contract" clearly indicates that the RMB 3,000,000 is compensation for losses, not liquidated damages. At the first-instance trial, it had been established that the appellee did not submit any evidence of having invested RMB 3,000,000, so this claim lacked any factual basis. The first-instance judgment, based on Article 28 of the "Company Law of the PRC", which stipulates that only a shareholder who has complied with its obligations can claim liability for breach of contract from a breaching shareholder, rejected all of the appellee's requests for liquidated damages. If the above RMB 3,000,000 were considered liquidated damages, the appellant should similarly not be liable. The joint venture company was already legally registered, which does not meet the condition of "cannot be registered" as stipulated in Article 14.3 of the "Joint Venture Contract", thus there is no basis for the appellant to bear liability. (2) The first-instance judgment, while not recognizing the equipment price for lack of supporting evidence, then used that same equipment price as the basis for ordering the appellant to pay 15% liquidated damages. This is not only contradictory but also violates legal provisions. The evidence submitted by the appellee in the first-instance trial lacked authenticity and relevance, was self-contradictory, and could not corroborate each other. For example, the formats of the contract originals and copies differed; the amount of equity pledged exceeded the number of issued capital shares; seven commercial receipts were too similar in elements such as font and signature; the dates of correspondence were unreasonable. All of these indicate a high probability that some or all of the evidence was forged. Based on the evidence submitted by the appellee, it was impossible to determine the true situation of the contract between the appellee and the seller, how much was paid for the equipment, or what liability for breach was incurred. It was precisely because the appellee's evidence could not prove its claims that the first-instance judgment did not recognize specific amounts including the equipment price. Yet, based on that same equipment price, it ordered the appellant to pay 15% liquidated damages, which is self-contradictory. Article 14.2 of the "Joint Venture Contract" specifically provides that liability for breach requires fault. However, the appellant was not at fault for not obtaining the land, and all evidence provided by the appellee could not prove any fault on the part of the appellant. In September and November 2007, the appellant orally and in writing notified the appellee of the "inability to complete the land procedures". This fulfilled its obligation to give timely notice and prevent the expansion of losses. The subsequent efforts to conduct remedial work under the organization of the competent authorities were also in fulfillment of the obligation to prevent loss expansion. The "Joint Venture Contract" and "Joint Venture Articles of Association" contain specific provisions on the termination of the joint venture company. The termination procedure should follow the law. The appellant's notice did not constitute a unilateral termination and had no connection to whether there was a breach of contract. According to the "Contract Law of the PRC", the specific methods of bearing liability for breach of contract can only be specific performance, remedial measures, liability for damages, or payment of liquidated damages. Among these, compensation for losses should be limited to actual losses, and the standard for adjusting liquidated damages is also the actual losses incurred. However, the first-instance judgment ordering the appellant to pay liquidated damages of RMB 6,788,420, being 15% of the equipment price, lacked any evidence of actual losses suffered by the appellee. This judgment violates relevant legal provisions. The object of the appellee's performance of its equipment contribution obligation is the joint venture company, not the appellant. The appellee provided equipment based on the actual needs of the joint venture company, not the actual needs of the appellant. The appellee purchased equipment to fulfill its contribution obligation, not for the benefit of the appellant. This has no connection to whether the appellant breached the contract. At the same time, the entity that notified the appellee to fulfill its equipment contribution obligation was the joint venture company, not the appellant. Therefore, the appellee should assert its rights against the joint venture company and has no right to assert against the appellant. It should not be compensated by other shareholders, including the appellant. For this claim, the appellee has no right of action against the appellant. The first-instance judgment ordered the appellant to bear liability based on the principle of fairness, but liability under the fairness principle cannot be liability for liquidated damages. (3) Article 28 of the "Company Law of the PRC" and Article 7 of the "Provisions on the Contributions of the Parties to Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures" and other laws and regulations clearly stipulate that only a shareholder who has fully paid its capital contribution on time and in full (the compliant party) can demand liability for breach of contract or damages from other breaching shareholders, and the breaching shareholders can only bear such liability to the compliant party. In this case, none of the shareholders of the joint venture company paid their capital contributions in full and on time as agreed or as required by law. Under these circumstances, no shareholder has the right to demand other shareholders bear liability for breach or damages. At the same time, Article 14.1 of the "Joint Venture Contract" also explicitly provides that liability for breach is owed to the "compliant party". The appellee, having itself seriously breached its capital contribution obligation, does not have the standing to hold other shareholders, including the appellant, liable for breach or damages. All of its claims lack legal basis. The amounts ordered in the first-instance judgment, whether liquidated damages or compensation, fall within the scope of liability for breach of contract, and the appellant should not bear them. (4) The reason the joint venture company could not obtain the land was due to government authorities. The appellant made its best efforts for the land-as-equity contribution and had no fault. The joint venture company and all shareholders suffered serious losses, but the cause was not the breach of any shareholder. All shareholders are victims. In these circumstances, making only one shareholder bear the consequences of loss clearly contradicts the facts of the case and relevant legal provisions. The joint venture company and its shareholders should assert their rights against the government. In summary, the first-instance judgment misapprehended the facts and erroneously applied the law. Request: 1. Set aside item 1 of the Civil Judgment (2008) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 12 of the Shanxi High People's Court, and amend to dismiss the appellee's claim under that item; 2. Set aside item 2 of the same judgment, and amend to hold that the appellant does not bear liquidated damages for equipment losses; 3. Affirm item 3 of the same judgment; 4. Order the appellee to bear all litigation costs.

Huanneng Company submitted a written opinion, stating: In November 2006, Huanneng Company, together with Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company, signed the "Joint Venture Contract" and "Joint Venture Articles of Association", jointly establishing Jiufang Company. Because Jincheng Company had invested certain human and material resources in preliminary work, the three parties agreed to convert this into RMB 3,000,000 and include it in the "Joint Venture Contract". After the signing of the "Joint Venture Contract", Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company took primary responsibility for handling the land contribution and equipment procurement, respectively. Because the procedures for land contribution progressed more slowly than anticipated, the cash contributions from the three joint venture parties were correspondingly postponed. The medical equipment purchased by Jincheng Company in Hong Kong was also temporarily held back from customs declaration. On February 25, 2007, the three joint venture parties signed a "Memorandum." This "Memorandum" required Cardiovascular Hospital to expedite the procedures for contributing the land as capital and to complete them before June of that year. It also confirmed that Jincheng Company had completed the equipment ordering as agreed, consented to Jincheng Company handling the customs declaration and related equipment investment work based on the actual operational situation of the project, agreed that cash would be injected in due course based on the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures, and also agreed that Huanneng Company would inject funds in stages according to project progress and the actual needs of the joint venture company's operations. Around late September of the same year, Cardiovascular Hospital suddenly orally informed Huanneng Company that the land use rights could not be obtained and that the cooperative project was ceasing operations. On January 22, 2008, Cardiovascular Hospital and Huanneng Company signed the "Memorandum on the Return of Investment Funds to Shanxi Huanneng Science and Trade Co., Ltd.", confirming that Cardiovascular Hospital would return RMB 2,619,700 to Huanneng Company on February 29, 2008. From the date of full return of the investment funds, Huanneng Company would withdraw from Jiufang Company and transfer all its rights and obligations in Jiufang Company to Cardiovascular Hospital. At this point, Huanneng Company had completely withdrawn from the three-party cooperation. The claims in the litigation between Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company are unrelated to Huanneng Company.

In response to Jincheng Company's appeal, Cardiovascular Hospital argued in its defense: (1) Jincheng Company did not pay its capital contributions in full and on time, making it a breaching party that does not have standing to claim liability for breach of contract against Cardiovascular Hospital. All of its claims lack legal basis. (2) The "Memorandum" substantially amended the capital contribution deadlines in the "Joint Venture Contract" and "Joint Venture Articles of Association" but was not approved by the approval authority. Therefore, it should be deemed not to have taken effect and cannot be used to determine the rights and obligations of the shareholders. Even if the "Memorandum" confirmed Jincheng Company's completion of equipment ordering, ordering is not the same as contributing capital. Jincheng Company never fulfilled its obligation to contribute equipment or cash, and the joint venture company never received the equipment or cash contributions from Jincheng Company. Jincheng Company's actions constitute a "breach in capital contribution." It cannot use the ineffective "Memorandum" to exempt itself from liability for breach of its capital contribution obligation. (3) Cardiovascular Hospital's written notice to Jincheng Company in November 2007 regarding the "inability to complete the land procedures" was an act of fulfilling its obligation to give timely notice and prevent the expansion of losses. Where the government competent authority had not approved the termination of the contract, Cardiovascular Hospital did not and had no right to unilaterally terminate the contract. Therefore, the notice does not constitute a unilateral termination and has no connection to whether there was a breach. (4) Jincheng Company's claim for dual application of Articles 14.1 and 14.3 of the "Joint Venture Contract" essentially amounts to double recovery. Calculating liquidated damages at 15% of the total registered capital has no contractual or legal basis. Jincheng Company itself is a breaching party. Under the circumstance that it lacks proper standing, demanding that Cardiovascular Hospital bear liability for breach has no factual or legal basis. (5) The "Order" has no relevance to this case and cannot prove the authenticity of the creditor-debtor relationship between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company; the evidence that the first-instance court required Jincheng Company to submit after the trial does not constitute new evidence and violates the provisions on evidence collection by the People's Court; the equipment purchase contract, commercial receipts, and other evidence relating to the equipment transaction provided by Jincheng Company cannot corroborate each other and are full of unreasonable contradictions. Therefore, its claim for compensation for the purchase price of the equipment and interest losses cannot stand. (6) Jincheng Company is also a breaching party and has no right to demand compensation for lost expected profits. Corporate operations are full of unknown factors. Jincheng Company's claim for compensation of RMB 10,000,000 for lost expected profits based on investment promotion advertisements and government documents has no factual or legal basis. In summary, all of Jincheng Company's claims lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed according to law.

Jincheng Company did not submit a written defense in response to Cardiovascular Hospital's appeal. At the trial, Jincheng Company argued: (1) The original judgment correctly ordered Cardiovascular Hospital to pay RMB 3,000,000 as liquidated damages. Jincheng Company had invested substantial preliminary work in the cooperative project, enabling the smooth progress of the early-stage work. These upfront investments constituted actual losses recognized by all three joint venture parties. Article 14.3 of the Joint Venture Contract stipulated that if Cardiovascular Hospital could not complete the land delivery, it should return RMB 3,000,000, and such obligation was not on the joint venture company. (2) Jincheng Company, at the request of Cardiovascular Hospital, entered into a contract with Baohe Company for the purchase of equipment. The original judgment's failure to recognize this due to minor defects in the evidence was erroneous. Minor discrepancies between the copy and the original of the contract should not negate the validity of the original. Regarding the determination of losses from equipment purchase, both Cardiovascular Hospital and Jincheng Company raised objections. Jincheng Company argued that the compensation should not be 15% of the amount already paid, but the total loss of over HKD 23,000,000 plus interest. The evidence from Baohe Company was provided by Jincheng Company at the request of the court of first instance and was evidence submitted within the designated period. Cardiovascular Hospital's refusal to examine this evidence during the first instance was unfair to Jincheng Company. (3) The "Order" of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is equivalent to a mediation statement and has legal effect. It should be recognized in the absence of evidence provided by the other party to negate its validity. (4) The "Memorandum" signed by the three joint venture parties required Jincheng Company to contribute capital based on the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. Each party was thus deemed to have fulfilled its capital contribution obligation. The Memorandum modified the original capital contribution obligations. Although it was not approved by the authorities, the party responsible for submitting for approval was Cardiovascular Hospital, and it was Cardiovascular Hospital that failed to complete the approval process. This case does not deal with external legal relations. When addressing internal issues of whether the parties breached the contract, the provisions of the Memorandum should apply. The Memorandum acknowledged that the equipment order had been completed and required Jincheng Company to make timely capital contributions based on the progress of the land contribution procedures. (5) The Joint Venture Contract stipulated that as long as the contribution of land as capital was not completed, liability for breach of contract would arise. Therefore, regardless of whether Cardiovascular Hospital was at fault, it should bear liability for breach. In summary, Cardiovascular Hospital's grounds for appeal lack factual basis and should be dismissed.

Regarding the facts found in the original judgment, Jincheng Company argued that the determination concerning the February 25, 2007 Memorandum omitted the fact that the third party, Huanneng Company, also made capital contributions based on the project's progress. This court finds: On February 25, 2007, the Memorandum signed by Jincheng Company, Cardiovascular Hospital, and the third party Huanneng Company included as item 3: "Party C (Huanneng Company) shall inject funds (cash) in stages based on the progress of this project and the actual operational needs of the joint venture company to ensure the company's early-stage operations." Therefore, Jincheng Company's above assertion is consistent with the facts, and this court affirms it.

Regarding the facts found in the original judgment, Cardiovascular Hospital argued that the determination that Cardiovascular Hospital instructed Jincheng Company to purchase equipment was not the true situation; rather, the equipment was purchased for the joint venture company. This court finds: On November 10, 2006, Cardiovascular Hospital sent a letter to Jincheng Company regarding the investment needs for imported equipment for the cooperative project, stating: "The main structure of the Cardiovascular Hospital inpatient building is now complete, and it is planned to be operational in October 2007. According to the cooperation agreement between the two parties, certain equipment should be directly procured and invested by your company. We are now providing a list of some equipment for your company, hoping you will arrange it as early as possible to ensure the smooth implementation of the project. The equipment list is as follows: 1. Positron Emission Tomography scanner, 1 unit, 20,000,000 each, total 20,000,000; 2. Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography scanner, 2 units, 3,600,000 each, total 7,200,000; 3. INTERACHIEVA 3.0 Magnetic Resonance Imaging system, 1 unit, 16,000,000 each, total 16,000,000; 4. BRILLIANCE CT 64-slice spiral CT, 1 unit, 15,000,000 each, total 15,000,000; 5. Flat panel detector angiography system, 4 units, 7,500,000 each, total 30,000,000; 6. Direct digital radiography system (dual plate), 2 units, 3,000,000 each, total 6,000,000; 7. Digital gastrointestinal machine, 1 unit, 2,500,000 each, total 2,500,000; 8. iU22 intelligent color ultrasound diagnostic system (abdominal machine), 5 units, 3,000,000 each, total 15,000,000; 9. iE33 intelligent cardiovascular ultrasound system (cardiac machine), 2 units, 3,000,000 each, total 6,000,000; 10. Biochemical analyzer, 3 units, 1,800,000 each, total 5,400,000; Total: 123,100,000 yuan." This letter set forth clear requirements for the names, quantities, unit prices, and total prices of the equipment to be ordered. Although the purpose was for the operation of the joint venture company, it is a fact that can be established that Cardiovascular Hospital sent a letter requesting Jincheng Company to arrange for the purchase of equipment as soon as possible. Therefore, Cardiovascular Hospital's denial that it instructed Jincheng Company to purchase equipment is inconsistent with the facts and is not supported by this court. The original judgment's finding of this fact was correct, and this court affirms it.

During the second instance, neither party submitted new evidence to this court. At the trial, neither party raised objections to other facts found in the original judgment. Accordingly, this court affirms the facts found in the original judgment. However, the original judgment omitted certain facts supported by evidence regarding the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's contribution of land use rights as capital and the payment of commissions and advance payments by Jincheng Company to Baohe Company. This court has ascertained and confirmed these facts during the second instance.

This court finds: On October 9, 2006, Cardiovascular Hospital submitted a "Request on the Agreement-based Transfer of State-owned Allocated Land for the Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Care, Rehabilitation Center Project" (Jin Xin Qing Zi [2006] No. 23) to the Shanxi Provincial Health Department, requesting submission to the Shanxi Provincial Department of Land and Resources for the agreement-based transfer of the state-owned allocated land belonging to the original trial court and the change in ownership for the contribution of land as capital. On October 16, 2006, the Shanxi Provincial Health Department submitted a "Request on the Agreement-based Transfer and Exemption from Land Transfer Fees for State-owned Allocated Land for the Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Care, Rehabilitation Center Project" (Jin Wei Qing [2006] No. 184) to the Shanxi Provincial Department of Land and Resources, applying for exemption from land transfer fees. On November 9, 2006, the Shanxi Provincial Department of Finance issued a "Reply on the Contribution of State-owned Land as Capital for the Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Care, Rehabilitation Center Project" (Jin Cai Zi [2006] No. 39), agreeing to Cardiovascular Hospital's contribution of land use rights as capital in the cooperative project and requiring an appraisal of the state-owned land to be contributed as capital in accordance with relevant regulations on the management of state-owned asset appraisal. On November 23, 2006, Shanxi Zhiyuan Real Estate Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd. submitted a "Land Appraisal Report" (Jin Zhi Yuan [2006] (Gu) Zi No. 087), appraising the price of Cardiovascular Hospital's state-owned allocated land use rights. On December 31, 2006, the Shanxi Provincial Department of Finance issued a "Notice on Approving the Land Use Rights Appraisal Project of Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Care, Rehabilitation Center" (Jin Cai Zi [2006] No. 47), approving the appraisal conduct and results of the appraisal agency, and deeming Cardiovascular Hospital's act of contributing land use rights as capital effective. On February 9, 2007, the Shanxi Provincial Development and Reform Commission issued a "Reply on Approving the Shanxi-Hong Kong Joint Venture Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Rehabilitation, Care Center Project" (Jin Fa Gai Wai Zi Fa [2007] No. 88), approving the project jointly invested by Cardiovascular Hospital, Jincheng Company, and Huanneng Company as requested by the Shanxi Provincial Health Department, and setting forth clear requirements for the total building area, total project investment, investment ratios, project operation mode, and term. On June 22, 2007, the Taiyuan City Planning Bureau issued a "Notice of Planning Design Conditions". On August 13, 2007, the Taiyuan City Bureau of Land and Resources issued a "Reply on the Pre-examination of Land Use for the Shanxi-Hong Kong Joint Venture Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Rehabilitation, Care Center Project" (Bing Guo Tu Zi [2007] No. 169), approving the pre-examination of land use and requiring Cardiovascular Hospital to handle relevant land use procedures such as land management, environmental protection, and geological hazard risk assessment in accordance with the law. Cardiovascular Hospital did not provide any evidence that it subsequently handled relevant land use procedures with relevant government departments, nor did it provide written evidence that relevant government departments refused to handle the relevant land use procedures.

Further found: The total price of the medical equipment sales contract signed between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company was HKD 112,457,261. Baohe Company issued seven "Formal Receipts" to Jincheng Company on November 22, November 23, November 28, December 13, December 18, December 19, and December 25, 2006, respectively. These seven "Formal Receipts" recorded that Baohe Company received from Jincheng Company an advance payment for the purchase of medical equipment of HKD 39,500,000 and a commission of HKD 5,622,800, totaling HKD 45,122,800. Lawyer Huang Guoxi, a China-appointed attesting officer, issued a "Certificate" certifying that the copies of the carbon paper counterfoil stubs of Baohe Company's receipts were consistent with the originals. This "Certificate" bore the forwarding seal of China Legal Services (Hong Kong) Limited.

This court, upon trial, finds:

(I) Regarding Jurisdiction and Applicable Law.

Jincheng Company, a party to this case, is incorporated in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, making this case a dispute over a Hong Kong-related joint venture contract. Article 18.1 of the Joint Venture Contract stipulates that all disputes arising from or in connection with the execution of this contract shall be settled through friendly negotiation between the parties; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to relevant judicial authorities for adjudication in accordance with the legal procedures of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the court of first instance properly exercised jurisdiction based on the parties' above agreement and the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 15 of the Implementation Rules of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures provides that the formation, validity, interpretation, execution, and dispute resolution of a joint venture contract shall be governed by the laws of China. This case is a dispute over a Hong Kong-related joint venture contract and should refer to this provision to determine the applicable law. Article 17.1 of the Joint Venture Contract signed by Jincheng Company, Cardiovascular Hospital, and the third party Huanneng Company stipulates that the formation, validity, interpretation, performance, and dispute resolution of this contract shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. This agreement complies with Article 15 of the Implementation Rules of the Law on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures. Therefore, this dispute should be resolved under the laws of Mainland China.

(II) Regarding the Validity of the Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association.

The Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association signed by Jincheng Company, Cardiovascular Hospital, and the third party Huanneng Company represent the true intentions of the three joint venture parties. Their contents do not violate legal provisions, and they were submitted for approval to the relevant approval authorities. They should be deemed legally valid.

(III) Regarding the Validity of the February 25, 2007 Memorandum.
