After signing the Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association, Jincheng Company, Cardiovascular Hospital, and the third party Huanneng Company signed a Memorandum concerning Jiufang Company on February 25, 2007, adjusting the timing and amount of capital contributions by the joint venture parties as stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract. Specifically, Cardiovascular Hospital was to complete the relevant land procedures by June of the same year; Jincheng Company was to handle the import customs clearance of equipment based on the actual progress of the project and inject funds in a timely manner based on the progress of the land procedures; Huanneng Company was to inject funds in stages based on the progress of the project and the actual operational needs of the joint venture company to ensure the company's early-stage operations. Considering that the approved Joint Venture Contract already had clear provisions on the capital contributions of each party, the three joint venture parties specifically agreed in the Memorandum that "all parties agree to adjust the timing and amount of capital contributions of the joint venture parties based on the actual progress of Party A's (Cardiovascular Hospital) land procedures, and by implementing in accordance with the above principles, all parties shall be deemed to have fulfilled their capital contribution obligations." However, because this Memorandum was not submitted to the relevant approval authority for approval, Jincheng Company and Cardiovascular Hospital hold differing views on its validity. This court finds: The Memorandum did change the timing and amount of capital contributions stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract. However, the background for the three parties signing the Memorandum was that Cardiovascular Hospital needed to go through planning, finance, land, and other approval procedures to contribute land use rights as capital. Its purpose was not to circumvent or change the approval matters of the approval authority but to more reasonably adjust the timing, amount, and sequence of the parties' capital contributions. The matters agreed upon in the Memorandum were not required to be submitted to the approval authority for approval and did not need further approval. The Memorandum was reached by the three joint venture parties on the basis of equality, voluntariness, and consensus. The adjustments it made to the parties' capital contributions were necessary and reasonable. Its contents reflected the true intentions of the joint venture parties and should be deemed legally valid and binding on all joint venture parties. Cardiovascular Hospital never raised any objection to the Memorandum or its validity before this lawsuit. Its assertion during the lawsuit that the Memorandum substantially modified the capital contribution deadlines stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association and should be deemed not in effect because it was not approved by the approval authority is inconsistent with the facts and relevant legal provisions, and this court does not support it.

(IV) Regarding the Party in Breach.

The cooperative project involved in this case was the only public health project signed at the "2006 Shanxi (Hong Kong) Investment Fair" for attracting foreign investment. Before formally signing the Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association, Jincheng Company and Cardiovascular Hospital first signed a "Letter of Intent for Cooperation" making preliminary agreements on the total investment, capital contribution, building area, operation mode, and responsibilities of the project. Jincheng Company also, based on the "Letter on Imported Equipment Investment Needs" provided by Cardiovascular Hospital, ordered the medical equipment specified by Cardiovascular Hospital from Baohe Company and paid commissions and advance payments as agreed. After signing the Joint Venture Contract and the Joint Venture Articles of Association, because Cardiovascular Hospital had not completed the procedures for contributing land use rights as capital, the three joint venture parties signed the Memorandum concerning Jiufang Company. This Memorandum not only confirmed the fact that Jincheng Company had already ordered medical equipment but also explicitly required Jincheng Company to handle the import customs clearance of equipment and related work for equipment investment based on the actual progress of the project and to inject cash in a timely manner based on the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. Accordingly, Jincheng Company negotiated with the seller Baohe Company to postpone the shipment of the medical equipment and did not inject further funds. It should be said that the substantial preliminary work and investments made by Jincheng Company for the cooperative project and the joint venture company, as well as the fact that it completed the equipment order in accordance with the contract and paid commissions and advance payments to the seller Baohe Company, all demonstrate that Jincheng Company not only had the sincerity to perform the contract but also engaged in substantive performance. The reason it did not strictly make capital contributions as stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract was that it was suspending or making timely capital contributions in compliance with the provisions of the Memorandum signed by the three joint venture parties, not to evade its capital contribution obligations under the Joint Venture Contract or the Joint Venture Articles of Association. Therefore, Jincheng Company should not be found in breach.

On the other hand, Cardiovascular Hospital failed to complete or timely complete the procedures for contributing land use rights as capital after signing the Letter of Intent for Cooperation, the Joint Venture Contract, and the Memorandum, thereby breaching its relevant commitments made in the Letter of Intent for Cooperation, the Joint Venture Contract, and the Memorandum. After orally notifying Jincheng Company that the cooperative project had ceased operation, Cardiovascular Hospital explicitly acknowledged in its letter of November 16, 2007, to Jincheng Company titled "Letter on the Termination and Implementation of the Shanxi Province Cardiovascular Disease Hospital and Elderly Care, Rehabilitation Center Project and Resolution of Aftermath Issues" that "due to unclear policy boundaries and other reasons, the land procedures could not be completed, leading to the termination of the project." Furthermore, in the "Memorandum on the Return of Investment Funds of Shanxi Huanneng Technology and Trade Co., Ltd." signed with Huanneng Company on January 22, 2008, Cardiovascular Hospital explicitly acknowledged "unilaterally terminating the project cooperation." Although Cardiovascular Hospital argued that the inability to complete the land use rights contribution procedures was due to government departmental reasons and that it was not at fault, it did not provide any written evidence from relevant government departments refusing or disagreeing to handle the land use rights contribution procedures. Because Cardiovascular Hospital did not continue to handle the relevant procedures, the cooperative project and the joint venture company had to cease operations due to the lack of land. In summary, the cause of this dispute is that Cardiovascular Hospital failed to complete the procedures for contributing land use rights as capital as stipulated in the Joint Venture Contract, thereby making it impossible to continue performing the Joint Venture Contract and causing the cooperative project and the joint venture company to cease operations. The original judgment, based on Article 28(1) of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, found that Jincheng Company's failure to contribute capital constituted a breach. This is clearly inconsistent with the facts that Jincheng Company ordered medical equipment and paid commissions and advance payments before signing the Joint Venture Contract and with the Memorandum's requirement to "inject funds in a timely manner" based on the progress of Cardiovascular Hospital's land procedures. Accordingly, the original judgment's finding that Jincheng Company breached the contract was improper and constituted an error in the application of law.

Cardiovascular Hospital, as a joint venture party, failed to fulfill its obligation to contribute the land use rights as capital. It should be found to have breached the contract in accordance with the law. The repayment agreement signed between Cardiovascular Hospital and the third party Huanneng Company explicitly acknowledged that Cardiovascular Hospital "unilaterally terminated the project operation," and Cardiovascular Hospital actually repaid Huanneng Company's investment funds. This demonstrates that Cardiovascular Hospital not only admitted its unilateral breach as a capital contributor to the cooperative project but also actually assumed liability for breach as the lead party of the cooperative project towards Huanneng Company. While Cardiovascular Hospital admitted unilateral breach and repaid Huanneng Company's investment, it denied breach and refused to compensate Jincheng Company for any losses. This is unfair to Jincheng Company. Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that if a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, it shall bear liability for breach, such as continuing performance, taking remedial measures, or compensating for losses. Jincheng Company's request, based on the Joint Venture Contract, that Cardiovascular Hospital bear liability for breach and compensate for losses complies with the above legal provisions, and this court supports it. The joint venture company, Jiufang Company, was not actually operated after its establishment and has no assets. Therefore, this dispute cannot and should not be resolved by claiming against Jiufang Company. Accordingly, Cardiovascular Hospital's argument that Jincheng Company should assert its rights against Jiufang Company lacks legal basis, and this court does not support it.

(V) Regarding the Probative Force of HCA 808/2008 "Order"

Since the Cardiovascular Hospital notified Jincheng Company orally and in writing that the cooperation project would cease operations, Jincheng Company immediately negotiated with Baohe Company regarding termination of the sales contract and compensation for breach of contract. As negotiations failed, Baohe Company filed a lawsuit in the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region demanding that Jincheng Company compensate for its losses. The High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region issued the aforesaid Order based on the settlement agreement reached between the parties. Accordingly, Jincheng Company shall pay Baohe Company compensation of HKD 23,622,800. Given that both Jincheng Company and Baohe Company are companies incorporated in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and that the total amount of commissions and advance payments Jincheng Company claims to have paid to Baohe Company already exceeds the total compensation amount required by the Order, there is no issue of enforcement of the Order, nor any issue requiring recognition and enforcement by a mainland court. In this case, the purpose of Jincheng Company submitting the Order is to use it as evidence to prove its losses from ordering medical equipment. Therefore, it is necessary to determine whether the Order has evidentiary effect.

The Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant mainland laws and regulations contain no provisions regarding whether an Order made by a court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region has evidentiary effect in mainland litigation proceedings. This Court holds that: whether the Order of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region can be admitted as evidence in the litigation of this case shall be examined in terms of its authenticity, legality, validity, and relevance. Jincheng Company submitted to the original trial court a notarized Legal Opinion issued by Ms. Gu Zhangwenju of the law firm Gu Zhang Wenju & Ye Chengqing. That Legal Opinion states: pursuant to Rule 5A of Order 42 of the Rules of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (Rules of the High Court), the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region has the authority to make the aforesaid Order based on the settlement agreement reached between the parties; such Order has the same effect as a court judgment or order; the requirement under Rule 5B of Order 42 of the Rules of the High Court regarding judgments with reasons does not apply to Orders made under Rule 5A of Order 42; and the Order is binding and enforceable against Jincheng Company and Baohe Company. Therefore, this Court confirms the authenticity, legality, and validity of the Order. As to whether it is relevant, this Court holds that the sales contract between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, the seven receipts issued by Baohe Company, the Memorandum signed by the three joint venture parties, the correspondence between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, the statement of claim of Baohe Company, and the litigation documents of the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region constitute a complete chain of evidence, sufficient to prove the facts that Jincheng Company ordered medical equipment and paid commissions and advance payments, that Jincheng Company negotiated with Baohe Company regarding the breach, that after negotiations failed a lawsuit was filed in the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and that the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region served litigation documents; it is also sufficient to prove that the Order is related to the dispute over the medical equipment sales contract between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company. Therefore, the Order is relevant to the dispute in this case. Furthermore, Jincheng Company completed relevant notarization and transmission procedures when submitting the Order, which complies with the provisions of Article 11, Paragraph 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation that "evidence provided by a party to a people's court that is formed in Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan shall fulfill relevant certification procedures." Therefore, in the absence of direct contrary evidence from the Cardiovascular Hospital, it shall be determined that the Order has probative value in this case, may be used as evidence, and the loss amount of Jincheng Company in ordering medical equipment shall be determined accordingly. The Cardiovascular Hospital's claim that the Order cannot prove the authenticity of the creditor-debtor relationship between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, and that the Order is not relevant to the dispute in this case, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. The Cardiovascular Hospital's claim that the compensation amount determined in the Order exceeded the 15% ratio promised by Baohe Company and that there may be collusion between the two parties lacks specific evidence, and this Court also does not support it.

(6) Regarding Jincheng Company's claim for liquidated damages.

In both the first and second instance proceedings, Jincheng Company claimed that the Cardiovascular Hospital should pay it liquidated damages for delayed capital contribution of RMB 2,814,750 and liquidated damages for termination of contract performance of RMB 22.5 million, pursuant to Articles 14.1 and 14.2 of the Joint Venture Contract respectively. However, the Cardiovascular Hospital's failure to handle the procedures for contributing land use rights as capital and causing the termination of the Joint Venture Contract is, in nature, not a delayed capital contribution but a fundamental breach, and therefore liquidated damages should not be paid according to the provision on delayed capital contribution in the Joint Venture Contract. Jincheng Company's claim that the Cardiovascular Hospital should pay liquidated damages for delayed capital contribution under Article 14.1 of the Joint Venture Contract has no basis, and this Court does not support it. Article 14.2 of the Joint Venture Contract provides for liability for breach of contract if, due to the fault of one joint venture party, the contract and its appendices cannot or cannot be fully performed; it is not a provision on liquidated damages. This article contains no provision regarding the ratio of liquidated damages, and Jincheng Company also failed to provide evidence proving that the parties ever reached an oral or written agreement to pay liquidated damages at 15% of the total registered capital of the Joint Venture Contract in case of breach. Therefore, Jincheng Company's claim that Article 14.2 of the Joint Venture Contract is a liquidated damages clause and its demand that the Cardiovascular Hospital pay it RMB 22.5 million in liquidated damages lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court also does not support it.

(7) Regarding the determination of Jincheng Company's loss amount.

In this case, the losses claimed by Jincheng Company include the principal of RMB 3 million in initial investment, interest on HKD 45.1228 million in commissions and advance payments paid to Baohe Company, the loss of compensation of HKD 23,622,800 paid to Baohe Company pursuant to the Order, and loss of prospective profits of RMB 10 million. These are discussed separately below.

Regarding the initial investment of RMB 3 million, the Cardiovascular Hospital appealed, arguing that Jincheng Company did not provide evidence proving it actually invested in the cooperation project or the joint venture company, and therefore it should not be supported; but Jincheng Company argued that the three parties had already clearly confirmed this initial investment in the Joint Venture Contract, so no further evidence was needed, and it should be supported. This Court holds that: Article 14.3 of the Joint Venture Contract stipulates, "After the parties sign this contract, if Party A fails to complete the procedures for contributing land as capital on time, causing the joint venture company to be unable to register, it shall be deemed as a breach. Proceed according to Article 14.1, and at the same time Party A shall return the RMB 3 million already invested by Party B and compensate for the losses from ordering equipment." This Joint Venture Contract reflects the true intentions of the three joint venture parties, has been approved by the relevant approval authority, and shall be determined as legal and valid. The contents recorded in the Joint Venture Contract shall be confirmed unless there is direct contrary evidence. The Memorandum signed by the three joint venture parties clearly confirms that each joint venture party made substantial work and contributions to the cooperation project and the joint venture company. The written opinion submitted by HuanNeng Company in the second instance proceedings clearly acknowledges that "because Jincheng Company made preliminary investments of certain manpower and material resources for preparatory work, the three parties agreed to convert this into RMB 3 million and include it in the Joint Venture Contract." The Cardiovascular Hospital also did not raise any objection within a reasonable time after signing the Joint Venture Contract. Therefore, it shall be determined that Jincheng Company made an initial investment of RMB 3 million in the cooperation project. When Jincheng Company filed the lawsuit at first instance, it did not claim interest on this amount, which shall be deemed as its waiver of the claim for interest on the initial investment. Although the original judgment determined that Jincheng Company had made an initial investment of RMB 3 million, the holding of the judgment erroneously characterized it as "liquidated damages for initial investment of RMB 3 million." This Court hereby corrects this error.

Regarding the commissions and advance payments of HKD 45.1228 million, the Cardiovascular Hospital appealed, arguing that the evidence submitted by Jincheng Company exhibits contradictions, such as inconsistencies between the copy and the original of the sales contract, lack of originals for receipts, contradictions between the contents of correspondence and the receipts, and contradictions between the dates and contents of relevant correspondence, and therefore it should not be recognized; Jincheng Company argued that the original sales contract should prevail, and the certificates and receipts issued by Baohe Company all show that Jincheng Company actually paid HKD 45.1228 million in commissions and advance payments, and therefore it should be recognized. This Court holds that: given the legal relationship of ordering medical equipment between Jincheng Company and Baohe Company, and the explicit provisions in the sales contract regarding total equipment amount, commissions, and advance payments, and further given that lawyer Huang Guoxi, a notary public commissioned by the Ministry of Justice, notarized that "the copy of the carbon copy stub of the receipt is consistent with the original document," therefore, in the absence of direct contrary evidence, the authenticity of Baohe Company's receipts shall be confirmed. Although the Cardiovascular Hospital claims that the evidence submitted by Jincheng Company has defects and believes Jincheng Company may have colluded with Baohe Company, it has not provided sufficient evidence to prove this, and this Court does not support this claim. The original judgment, on the one hand, did not recognize that Jincheng Company paid HKD 45.1228 million in commissions and advance payments to Baohe Company, but on the other hand, used this amount as the basis to calculate the amount of liquidated damages the Cardiovascular Hospital should pay, which is both self-contradictory and lacks basis. This Court hereby corrects this. Both Jincheng Company and the Cardiovascular Hospital appealed the above determination in the original judgment. This Court holds that the objections raised by both appellants on this point are correct. Therefore, Jincheng Company's claim that the Cardiovascular Hospital should pay it interest on HKD 45.1228 million is supported. When Jincheng Company filed the lawsuit, it claimed the interest on this amount should start from December 25, 2006, and this Court confirms this.

Regarding the compensation of HKD 23,622,800, since the Order has probative value in this case, it shall be determined as belonging to Jincheng Company's losses from ordering medical equipment. However, Article 119, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that after one party breaches the contract, the other party shall take appropriate measures to prevent the loss from expanding; if it fails to take appropriate measures, causing the loss to expand, it may not claim compensation for the expanded loss. The letter from Baohe Company to Jincheng Company dated January 4, 2008, indicates that Baohe Company agreed to calculate compensation based on 15% of the total sales contract amount of HKD 112,457,261. However, the compensation amount determined in the settlement agreement reached during the litigation in the High Court of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region exceeded the compensation amount previously promised by Baohe Company. In this regard, Jincheng Company was at fault and, according to law, has no right to claim compensation from the Cardiovascular Hospital for the expanded loss. Therefore, the Cardiovascular Hospital shall pay Jincheng Company compensation calculated at 15% of the above total sales contract amount.

Regarding the loss of prospective profits of RMB 10 million, Jincheng Company argued that based on the project approval document Jin Fa Gai Wai Zi [2007] No. 88 issued by the Shanxi Provincial Development and Reform Commission, the benefits that the cooperation project and Jincheng Company as a shareholder could obtain can be calculated, and that claiming only RMB 10 million is reasonable and should be supported; the Cardiovascular Hospital argued that Jincheng Company did not consider project risks and calculated prospective profits based on investment advertisements and government documents, which is unreasonable and should not be supported. This Court holds that: although Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the compensation for losses caused by one party's breach may include the benefits obtainable after performance of the contract, in this case, the funds required for the cooperation project and the joint venture company were not fully in place, and the cooperation project and the joint venture company were not actually operated, so there was no profit at all. Moreover, whether a joint venture company is profitable depends on many factors. Therefore, Jincheng Company's reliance solely on government documents to claim that it should receive RMB 10 million in compensation for prospective profits lacks sufficient basis, and this Court does not support it. The Cardiovascular Hospital's defense on this ground is valid, and this Court supports it.

Furthermore, the Cardiovascular Hospital also argued that according to Article 14.3 of the Joint Venture Contract, the precondition for returning the initial investment and compensating for losses from ordering equipment is "failure to complete the procedures for contributing land as capital on time, causing the joint venture company to be unable to register." However, in this case, the joint venture company, Jiufang Company, had already been registered and established, so Jincheng Company's claim for the return of initial investment and compensation for losses from ordering equipment fails because the precondition of "inability to register the joint venture company" is not met. This Court holds that: the Cardiovascular Hospital's breach in this case constitutes a fundamental breach, and the result of its breach directly caused the joint venture company to be unable to continue operations and the purpose of the joint venture to be unattainable. Although Article 14.3 of the Joint Venture Contract stipulates the precondition of "inability to register the joint venture company," this is not the only condition for the Cardiovascular Hospital to bear liability for breach of contract. Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates the liability for breach of contract that the breaching party shall bear. The Cardiovascular Hospital, as the breaching party, shall bear liability for breach according to law. Therefore, this Court does not support the Cardiovascular Hospital's above argument.

In summary, the appeal grounds of the appellant Jincheng Company regarding liquidated damages, expanded losses from ordering medical equipment, and loss of prospective profits are all untenable, and this Court does not support them. However, the losses of interest on commissions and advance payments and partial losses from ordering medical equipment caused by the Cardiovascular Hospital's breach shall be supported. The appeal grounds of the appellant Cardiovascular Hospital that it should bear no liability for the initial investment, interest on commissions and advance payments, and losses from ordering medical equipment are all untenable, and this Court does not support them. The original judgment is partially unclear in fact-finding and improperly applied the law. This Court hereby corrects it. Pursuant to Articles 8, 44, 60, 107, and 119 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The Civil Judgment of the Shanxi High People's Court (2008) Jin Min Chu Zi No. 12 is set aside;

2. Shanxi Provincial Cardiovascular Disease Hospital shall pay Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. the initial investment of RMB 3 million within 30 days after this judgment takes effect;

3. Shanxi Provincial Cardiovascular Disease Hospital shall pay Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. the loss from ordering medical equipment of HKD 16,868,589.15 within 30 days after this judgment takes effect;

4. Shanxi Provincial Cardiovascular Disease Hospital shall pay Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd. the interest loss on the commissions and advance payments of HKD 45.1228 million (calculated at the Hong Kong dollar lending rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, from December 25, 2006 to July 24, 2008) within 30 days after this judgment takes effect;

5. Hong Kong Jincheng Investment Co., Ltd.'s other claims are dismissed.

If the monetary obligation determined in this judgment is not performed within the specified period, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
